newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK GRAFT BUSTERS NAB 18 IN HORSE RACE FIXING.
newsitem.headline: HK GRAFT BUSTERS NAB 18 IN HORSE RACE FIXING.

text.p: Hong Kong graft-busters have arrested 18 people, including four jockeys and two trainers in connection with illegal bookmaking and syndicated horse race fixing.

The Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) said in a statement issued late on Sunday they also searched fifty-five premises, including two which were suspected to be illegal bookmaking centres, involving some 220 anti-graft fighters.
The arrests followed an investigation after the ICAC received information from the Hong Kong Jockey Club and complaints from the public, the ICAC said.
The anti-graft fighters gave no further details, saying enquiries were to continue.
Sunday's swoop was the biggest since 1986 when 22 people were arrested for alleged involvement in a syndicate controlling more than 75 horses and a number of jockeys and trainers.
As the only legal outlet for a flutter in gambling-mad Hong Kong, the Jockey Club had a turnover of more than HK$80 billion (US$11 billion) in 1995.
